question: Regulation (EU) 2021/817 (Articles 3 and 15), the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights (Articles 21 and 26) and the strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities 2021-2030 require Member States to ensure equality, accessibility and inclusiveness with regard to the participation of students with disabilities in education, school services, transport and sport activities.

Despite these legal obligations, recent reports show that significant shortcomings persist in Greece in relation to accessible school infrastructure and specialised staff, as well as to the safe transport of students with disabilities and their systematic inclusion in sports activities. These findings raise legitimate concerns as to the full implementation of EU requirements. The Commission is asked: 1.

How does it assess Greece’s level of compliance with Articles 21 and 26 of the Charter and with Regulation (EU) 2021/817, in particular as regards the accessibility of school infrastructure and the transport and participation of students with disabilities in school and sports activities?

What is the timeline for the implementation of the EU strategy for the rights of persons with disabilities 2021-2030, and with what tools will the Commission support Member States in ensuring adequate infrastructure and specialised staff, in line with the regulation and the Charter?
To what extent can the Commission support Greece in developing systematic mechanisms to monitor and improve accessibility for students with disabilities?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.3.2026) The Commission ensures compliance with the Charter of Fundamental Rights1 of measures under EU competence2. According to Article 51(1), the Charter applies to Member States when implementing EU law.

3 In line with the enabling conditions set in the Common Provisions Regulation4, action supported by EU funding must comply with the Charter’s provisions and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities5. These conditions are considered fulfilled by Greece.

The Erasmus+ programme6 prioritises learners with fewer opportunities and supports development of innovative teaching materials enhancing inclusion as well as building capacities. The implementation of the Strategy for the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2021-20307 is ongoing and the Strategy will be enhanced as of 20268.

EU cohesion policy supports accessible and inclusive education, in line with initiatives under the European Education Area (EEA) such as Pathways to School Success9. In Greece, under EU Cohesion Policy, support for children with disabilities has been expanded by recruiting special education teachers through co-financing granted by the European Social Fund+10.

The European Regional Development Fund has allocated approximately EUR 495 million for upgrading education infrastructure through 13 regional programmes. The Recovery and Resilience Facility supports a pilot programme on early interventions for children with disabilities11 and customized educational programmes are planned under the European Child Guarantee12.
Finally, the Commission monitors education policies under the EEA13.
1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/treaty/char_2016/oj/eng. 2 In the area of education, the EU has the competence “to carry out actions to support, coordinate or supplement

the actions of the Member States”, in line with the repartition of competences set out in Article 165 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/treaty/tfeu_2008/art_165/oj/eng.

3 Moreover, Article 6(1) of the Treaty of the European Union states that, ‘the provisions of the Charter shall not extend in any way the competences of the Union as defined in the Treaties’: https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/treaty/teu_2016/art_6/oj/eng. 4 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/1060/oj/eng. 5 https://www.ohchr.org/en/instruments-mechanisms/instruments/convention-rights-persons-disabilities.

11 https://op.europa.eu/en/publication-detail/-/publication/30c1ccaa-bfdd-11f0-a612-01aa75ed71a1/language-en. 12 National action plans and progress reports, including for Greece are available at: https://employment-socialaffairs.ec.europa.

eu/policies-and-activities/social-protection-social-inclusion/addressing-poverty-and-supportingsocial-inclusion/investing-children/european-child-guarantee/national-action-plans-and-progress-reports_en. 13 More in particular through the annual Education and Training Monitor: https://op.europa.eu/webpub/eac/education-and-training-monitor/en/.
